To find ${f}^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y:$

$$
y=\frac{3}{\sqrt[3]{2x-1}}+2
$$

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

$$
x=\frac{3}{\sqrt[3]{2y-1}}+2.
$$

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{3}{\sqrt[3]{2y-1}}+2 \\ \sqrt[3]{2y-1} & =\frac{3}{x-2} \\ (\sqrt[3]{2y-1})^{3} & ={(\frac{3}{x-2})}^{3} \\ 2y-1 & =\frac{27}{(x-2)^{3}} \\ 2y & =\frac{27}{(x-2)^{3}}+1 \\ y & =\frac{27}{2(x-2)^{3}}+\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the inverse function is 

$$
{f}^{-1}(x)=\frac{27}{2(x-2)^{3}}+\frac{1}{2}.
$$

**Note**: The domain and range of $f(x)$ are

$$
x\ne \frac{1}{2},\,f(x)\ne 2.
$$

Therefore, the domain and range of ${f}^{-1}(x)$ are

$$
x\ne 2,\,{f}^{-1}(x)\ne \frac{1}{2}.
$$
